paragraphs: A milling machine removes material rather than adding it, which is still how most precise metal parts are made despite everything printing has promised. The touchscreen on the front is the newest part of a machine whose geometry has not fundamentally changed in a century.

The model holds 107,172 polygons and 116,454 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the axes and doors can be posed or animated. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $99 it suits manufacturing and workshop visualisation, machine tool marketing, training and safety material, technical presentation, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The kneeler is a piece of church furniture designed to be uncomfortable enough to keep you awake and no more. A figure using one properly, weight forward and hands together, gives an interior render something no amount of architectural detail can: a reason for the room to exist.
The character holds 28,785 polygons and 23,511 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in the kneeling pose, and carries StemCell certification.
At $99 it suits architectural and interior visualisation, religious and historical scenes, education and documentary work, film previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Raven is thrown by hand like a paper aeroplane and lands by breaking apart on purpose, then being clipped back together. It is the smallest useful drone in military service, carried in a rucksack and flown by whoever happens to need to see over the next hill.

The airframe is very light at 21,858 polygons and 23,092 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps, 3 at 8192x8192 and 4 at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $99 it suits defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

A road bike is the most weight obsessed object most people will ever own. Every tube shape, every hole drilled and every component choice is an argument about grams, and the geometry is set by how far forward a rider is willing to be bent for several hours.

The model holds 114,245 polygons and 111,817 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 16 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $99 it suits cycling and sports visualisation, product and retail imagery, advertising, street and architectural scenes, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

The retro scooter sells a memory rather than a specification. Rounded panels, chrome mirrors and a step through frame borrowed from the fifties, wrapped around a modern engine that is quieter and more reliable than anything the original ever had.

The model holds 104,199 polygons and 106,516 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $99 it suits urban and street visualisation, motorcycle marketing, advertising and lifestyle imagery, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

The XM7 was adopted to solve a problem that had been argued about for decades: modern body armour that older infantry rounds cannot defeat. The rifle is larger and heavier than what it replaces, and the whole programme is a deliberate trade of ammunition weight for penetration.
The model holds 179,064 polygons and 179,805 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is enough for close inspection, and carries StemCell certification.
At $99 it suits defence visualisation and presentation, documentary and news graphics, game weapons, film props, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The dhow is one of the oldest hull forms still working. A lateen sail, a planked hull sewn or nailed depending on the century, and a shape that carried the Indian Ocean trade long before Europe arrived in it. Worn and used is how they almost always look.
The model holds 122,614 polygons and 128,299 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, in aged condition, and carries StemCell certification. A Bahraini fishing dhow is offered separately.
At $99 it suits maritime and cultural visualisation, historical and documentary work, tourism imagery, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A stretcher trolley is a machine for moving a person who cannot help. It has to fold to enter a vehicle, lock at several heights, take a patient's full weight on one end while being lifted at the other, and do all of it in seconds with one person if necessary.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the trolleys as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $89 the set suits healthcare and emergency services visualisation, medical equipment marketing, training material, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The Ark is described in more construction detail than almost anything else in the Hebrew Bible: dimensions, materials, the gold inside and out, the rings for the poles. It is one of the few sacred objects for which a specification survives, and every depiction is an interpretation of that text.
The model holds 144,346 polygons and 150,814 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $89 it suits religious and historical visualisation, museum and exhibition work, education and documentary material, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

Borgund is the best preserved stave church in Norway, built entirely of wood standing on end rather than laid flat, which is what stave means. The dragon heads on the gables are older than the Christianity the building was raised for, and nobody removed them.
The model is supplied in a snowy winter setting, in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.

At $89 it suits architectural and heritage visualisation, tourism and travel imagery, historical and documentary work, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A modern cattle shed is designed around airflow more than shelter. The open sides, the ridge vent and the height of the roof are all there to keep air moving over a large number of animals, because heat and damp cause far more losses than cold ever does.
The model holds 868,145 polygons and 896,628 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, suited to the repeated structure and fittings. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits agricultural and livestock visualisation, farm building presentation, equipment and welfare material, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Coatlicue is a mother goddess rendered as something deliberately terrifying: a skirt of serpents, a necklace of hands and hearts, and no head at all. The statue was dug up in Mexico City, reburied because it disturbed people, and dug up again.
The model is light at 10,957 polygons and 11,157 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to museum scenes and background use, and carries StemCell certification.

At $89 it suits museum and exhibition work, historical and archaeological visualisation, education and documentary material, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A construction printer is a gantry that extrudes concrete in layers, and the ribbed walls it leaves behind are the honest signature of the process. It builds the shell fast and cheaply; everything else about the house still has to be done the old way.
The model holds 614,101 polygons and 672,223 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $89 it suits construction technology visualisation, equipment marketing, architectural and innovation presentation, documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

Whole body screening is a piece of equipment that has to be both effective and unthreatening, because the person walking into it has no choice. The design work is mostly about making a radiation cabinet look like a doorway.

The model is light at 31,477 polygons and 33,304 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to interior scenes where it is one element among many. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $89 it suits security and screening visualisation, airport and facility presentation, equipment marketing, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2021.
